errors.text: The proposed Si intervention is not supported by the cited evidence, which concerns Laves formation in Cr/V-containing refractory alloys rather than Si-modified Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Hf2Si and Mo2Si are silicides, not C15 AB2 Laves phases; labeling them as a C15 Laves network is a fundamental phase-chemistry error.
The density prediction is physically reversed: Si is much lighter than every constituent of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr, so dilute Si addition cannot increase density because of its higher atomic mass.
The mechanical predictions use uniform elongation for a room-temperature compression problem and employ unsupported baseline strength, strain, and density values.
The baseline-versus-Si experiment does not isolate solid-solution hardening from phase-network effects because solute content, heat treatment, and phase state all change simultaneously.
